It was left unedited so the fact it was tried survives.
lap2.the_mistake_this_lap_made_and_caught: The same lap repaired read-gumroad.mjs's file_count (it asked Array.isArray on an object, so it had been null on every reading ever taken) and the repair GUESSED TOO: it counted object keys as files and emitted file_count 1. The live reading came back keys ["Size"] — a metadata label, not a file. A product with ten files would have reported 1 identically. Now null, with the raw shape and keys recorded where they cannot be read as a count. Shape-agnostic code still has to meet the real shape before its output is trusted.

lap3.what_it_deliberately_does_not_do: Open a lane. Inventing an escape hatch is a design decision and belongs to a lap that argues for it in the open, the way route_change was argued for. This lap made the closure data so the next context finds a measured fact instead of rediscovering a sentence. It PRINTS rather than fails: red here would mean 'the world has not produced revenue yet', which no lap fixes by working harder. The closure lifts by itself the moment a channel goes finite, and the suite asserts that it does.
